name: Igal
overview: Igal was a male warrior known as the son of Nathan and recognized as the thirty-first member of "the thirty," an elite group of King David's mighty men. His tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture. Beyond his role as one of David's distinguished soldiers, little else is recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Igal means "he redeems," reflecting a Hebrew root that conveys deliverance or redemption. Additionally, he is also called Joel in another biblical reference, a name meaning "YHWH is God [El]," highlighting a theistic affirmation. Neither name is indicated as being divinely given.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Igal as the son of Nathan. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Igal's significance lies in his inclusion among David's elite warriors, "the thirty," marking him as a figure of valor and loyalty during David's reign. Being the thirty-first of this distinguished group underscores his notable role in the king's military leadership. His mention preserves the memory of those who served faithfully under God's anointed king, contributing to the biblical narrative of God's providence through David's mighty men.
